walkthroughs.body_html:
Light travels in straight lines, so when an opaque object blocks it, the area behind has no light - a shadow.

A bigger object or closer light makes a bigger shadow.

Eclipses are giant shadows: the Moon's shadow on Earth (solar eclipse) or Earth's shadow on the Moon (lunar eclipse).

Refraction is when light bends as it enters a new medium (like water or glass).

Going from air to water: light slows down and bends towards the normal.

This is why a straw in a glass of water looks broken at the surface.

Refraction also lets lenses focus light in glasses, cameras, and your eye!

White light is a mix of 7 colours: Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Indigo, Violet.

A prism splits white light into this spectrum - because each colour refracts by a slightly different amount.

Rainbows form when sunlight hits water droplets - they act like millions of tiny prisms.

mcqs.q: Why does a straw in water look bent?
options: Water magnifies it
Light reflects off water
Light refracts at the surface
Eyes get confused

mcqs.q: A prism splits white light into.
options: Only red and blue
A spectrum of seven colours
Black and white
Nothing - it doesn't change

mcqs.q: Why is gravitational potential energy near a planet treated as negative?
options: Gravitational potential energy is negative because gravity does negative work.
Gravitational potential energy is negative because gravity always points downwards.
Electrons are sometimes waves and sometimes particles depending on the temperature of the apparatus.
Because the zero is defined at infinity; objects bound to the planet have lower (negative) potential energy than at infinity.

mcqs.q: If a car doubles its speed, what happens to its kinetic energy?
options: Kinetic energy stays the same because mass hasn't changed.
Electrons are sometimes waves and sometimes particles depending on the temperature of the apparatus.
Kinetic energy doubles because energy is proportional to speed.
It quadruples (because KE = 1/2 mv^2 — kinetic energy is proportional to v^2).

mcqs.q: When does an electron behave as a wave?
options: Kinetic energy stays the same because mass hasn't changed.
Electrons are sometimes waves and sometimes particles depending on the temperature of the apparatus.
Electrons are always waves and only look like particles at low energy.
In experiments that probe wave properties (e.g. diffraction through a crystal); in particle-like experiments it behaves as a particle.
